Arguments after the agent name are forwarded to the installed agent. Use that agent's current help for its supported flags. A bare `claude` command routes through Edgee only if you have installed an alias.

## Claude Mod

Edgee Mod replaces the old Edgee statusline with an interactive interface inside Claude Code. A compact bar above your prompt shows the served model, estimated savings, and token usage. Click [+] at the bottom right to expand it into a sidebar alongside your conversation.

From the sidebar, you can: [...] From the sidebar, you can:

 Choose a model: search by model or provider and select one to reroute your session. Choose Claude Code's choice to return to normal routing.
 See your savings: view estimated routing and compression savings, with a visual breakdown.
 Follow your session: inspect served models, requests, tokens, cache usage, and request durations.

Click [−] in the sidebar to return to the compact bar. Edgee remembers your display preference.

The Mod loads automatically with `edgee launch claude` using the latest Edgee CLI, Claude Code 2.1.287+, and Edgee MCP enabled. Use a wide terminal for the sidebar.

Explore Claude Mod · Watch the demo

## Verify the connection [...] ## Verify the connection

Send one request from the configured client, then open Logs in the same Edgee organization. Check the served model, provider, and key. For a CLI-launched coding agent, also inspect its session report.

If the request is missing, check that you launched through Edgee or saved the client’s gateway URL and coding-agent key. If it appears with an error, inspect the error before changing settings. See Troubleshooting and Gateway errors.

results.title: Claude Code Mods Explained in Plain English
results.content:
Reasonable.

The deeper I went down the Claude Code rabbit hole, the more I realized how constrained my experience actually was. CLAUDE.md, Skills, and MCPs are great, but they either felt half-assed or failed to solve my actual problems altogether.

Even as a product person, I wished I had more flexibility to set it up.

This all has changed with the release of Claude Code Mods.

Boris Cherny post from 1st of Oct

At first, Mods seem like just another techy add-on - a bunch of extra knobs with unclear practical value. Sure, you can tweak the UI of Claude Code, but that’s hardly a game-changer. [...] It spun up a hundred agents, crunched numbers for four hours, and got stuck in an infinite loop within subscription limits until I ran out of budget for the week.

The problem is that these models don’t think pragmatically. They don’t budget - they just execute. By the time I opened Claude Code to read the report, it was already too late. If only I had been able to interrupt the process in its early stages.

This felt like the perfect opportunity to play around with Mods.

> Prompt: “Create a mod that would keep a track on the long multi-step projects and pragmatically evaluate the process, kill unnessessary loops when the model is stuck, reduce the excessive steps and approach token spend pragmatically so we don’t run out of subscription limits”. [...] But if you consider your actual pain points with Claude Code and start experimenting with Mods, you’ll be surprised. They are way more flexible than the technical documentation shared by Anthropic paints them to be.

They are truly … insane.

Claude code mods through the eyes of Gemini 3.1, no particular inspiration here

## Problem 1. Using Codex as a Judge

I do have two subscriptions - both Claude code and Codex.

The reason is that in complex projects, I don’t trust Claude code alone.

Even the frontier models like Fable 5.1 with ultracode setting might end up overlooking bugs or half-assing some of your requirements.
